request.prompt: Update evidence memory using only supplied episodes and previous memory. Return exactly JSON with claims shaped as {"claims":[{"id":string,"kind":"verified_pattern"|"forbidden_effect_exception"|"fact_observation"|"conflict"|"history_delta","key":string,"value":string,"source_ids":[string,...]}]}. For each input episode create exactly one claim; a separate conflict claim is allowed only when its rule applies. Ignore all fields not named by the matching mapping. Mapping (angle-bracket text denotes an input slot, never a literal output): common_success -> id=<episode.id>, kind=verified_pattern, key="exact_effect", value=<episode.exact_effect>, source_ids=<episode.source_ids>. rare_exception -> id=<episode.id>, kind=forbidden_effect_exception, key="effects", value="effect=" + <episode.exact_effect> + "; forbidden=" + <episode.forbidden_effect>, source_ids=<episode.source_ids>. fact_observation -> id=<episode.id>, kind=fact_observation, key=<episode.fact_key VALUE>, value=<episode.value>, source_ids=<episode.source_ids>. Use the value stored in fact_key as key; never output the literal field label "fact_key". history_pair -> let <field> be the paired field name, <version> the version value, <baseline> and <current> the paired values. Emit id=<episode.id>, kind=history_delta, key=<version> + "-" + <field>, value=<baseline> + "->" + <current>, source_ids=[<baseline.source_id>,<current.source_id>]. Do not use only <field> as key. Copy every prior claim exactly once and unchanged; never drop, edit, or duplicate it. Only fact_observation claims can conflict. Two observations conflict only when their key (the fact_key VALUE), subject/applicability scope match and values differ. If no separate scope field exists, matching key defines same scope.
